As a logistical inventory specialist, you strengthen the team of order pickers at Kuehne+Nagel in Geel working in 2 shifts for €16,3753/hour and meal vouchers.

You fulfill a versatile key position as a logistical inventory specialist, combining the physical order picking of famous toy products with the administrative follow-up of inventory and quality controls. Thanks to your sharp eye and accurate way of working, your contribution as a logistical inventory specialist guarantees a flawless logistical process.

Ready to take the next step as an order picker? Aply via talentcenter1@randstad.be or 011 54 92 85!

VG 458/BUOSAP

Who are we looking for?

• At least 6 months of demonstrable experience within the logistics sector.
• Practical experience with a hand scanner and administrative follow-up.
• Good command of either the Dutch or English language.
• Willingness to work in a 2-shift system.
• Possession of your own transport to reach the location in Geel.
Key responsibilities

• Physically collecting toy goods and orders using a hand scanner.
• Performing thorough quality checks on picked orders from colleague order pickers.
• Monitoring stock levels and supporting warehouse administration.
• Spotting and correcting inventory discrepancies at an early stage.

Join Kuehne+Nagel in Geel as an experienced order picker and earn €16,3753/hour plus €8 meal vouchers working in a 2-shift system! In this varied role, you will combine active order picking with quality control and warehouse administration. You will ensure top quality for renowned brands and make sure every shipment is in perfect condition.

Ready to take the next step in your logistics career? Send your CV to talentcenter1@randstad.be or call us directly at 011 54 92 85!

VG 458/BUOSA

• Minimum of 6 months to 1 year of experience in a warehouse setting or order picking.
• Proven experience working with a handheld scanner is required.
• Good command of either Dutch or English.
• Willing to work in a 2-shift rotation on a long-term basis.
• Must have your own transport to commute to the site in Geel.

• Order picking goods in the warehouse using a handheld scanner.
• Conducting accurate quality control checks on picked orders.
• Checking and monitoring physical inventory and stock discrepancies.
• Handling the required warehouse administration within the system.
• Reporting deviations and safeguarding overall quality standards.

Are you an experienced order picker looking for a new logistics challenge? Join Kuehne+Nagel in Beringen! Do you have experience in logistics and a natural talent for leadership?

For a modern logistics company, we are looking for a Team Leader who can lead, motivate, and support the warehouse team while contributing daily to the smooth operation of all logistics activities.

Your Role: The Driving Force Behind the Team

As a Team Leader, you are the first point of contact for a team of warehouse operators. You ensure that all processes, from receiving goods to shipping orders, are carried out safely, efficiently, and accurately. You motivate your team, provide guidance when needed, and maintain a clear overview of daily operations.
Your Responsibilities:

 
• Leading, coaching, and supporting the logistics team on the warehouse floor
 
• Coordinating daily warehouse activities and resolving operational challenges
 
• Monitoring planning, safety, and quality standards
 
• Collaborating with other departments and proactively contributing solutions
 
• Rolling up your sleeves and assisting with operational tasks when required

 
• You have leadership experience and know how to motivate people in a positive and constructive way.
 
• You have strong communication skills and are flexible.
 
• You are fluent in English.
 
• You have experience leading a team and hold a valid forklift and/or reach truck certificate.
 
• You enjoy working in a dynamic environment with changing priorities.
 
• You are willing to work in a two-shift system or on a fixed night shift.

Job Description

In this hands-on position with the European Customer Analytical Services - Technology Centre of Excellence, you will perform root cause investigations into metallurgical failures and assess corrosion mechanisms. Serving clients throughout Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, you will analyze samples from hydrocarbon process and water treatment operations-such as petroleum refineries, cooling towers, heat exchangers, and boilers. Your expertise in metallurgy and failure analysis will directly drive critical materials and reliability decisions across water and hydrocarbon process systems.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Conduct comprehensive metallurgical failure analyses and corrosion mechanism assessments, gathering necessary process information and determining required analytical approaches to determine root causes of failures in industrial water and hydrocarbon process systems

• 
Act as the technical go-to for metallurgical evaluations and materials selection, providing consulting support across the organization

• 
Operate the Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM-EDXA) and other analytical instrumentation to support metallurgical examinations

• 
Execute failure analysis investigations on membrane systems (reverse osmosis, ultra-/nanfiltration membranes, flat sheet and spiral wound, as well as hollow fibre configurations), delivering clear findings and recommendations

• 
Collaborate with other laboratory departments (organic analyses, microbiological examinations, etc.) to gather comprehensive analytical data

• 
Prepare detailed, professional analytical reports and provide high-level technical input to Technology and Commercial teams

• 
Deliver work on schedule in a fast-paced, high-volume environment while maintaining compliance with all EHS policies and procedures

• 
Take ownership of customer application and R&D projects on membrane systems, including planning, execution, and reporting

• 
Master's degree in Metallurgical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, or equivalent professional experience

• 
Minimum 3 years of metallurgical laboratory experience, including leading failure analysis investigations (academic and/or industrial/commercial)

Oversee contractor-led tool installations for the Málaga cleanroom (Fab 5) project, with a focus on safety and conformity with imec’s standards and guidelines. 

 

What you will doFor the Málaga Fab 5 project, tool installations will be performed by the contractor. imec’s role focuses on safety oversight and validating that the installations conform to imec’s required standards and guidelines. That’s where you come in. Onboarding and training will take place in Leuven, Belgium until mid-2028, after which the position location will transfer to Málaga, Spain.  
As Project Lead, your role combines contractor oversight, safety follow-up and installation conformity validation on behalf of imec. 
The contractor is responsible for installation execution and day-to-day coordination of the installation works. You will monitor progress, review safety and quality matters, and coordinate interfaces with imec stakeholders, keeping a clear distinction between contractor execution and imec oversight. 
Your focus is to validate conformity with imec’s installation standards, guidelines and safety requirements. You will review contractor deliverables and installation evidence, follow up deviations and corrective actions, and support installation acceptance by imec rather than directly managing execution. 
You will: 
 
 

• Oversee contractor-led installations and coordinate interfaces with imec 

• Review contractor schedules and monitor progress against agreed milestones 

• Flag scope deviations and their impact on timelines, budgets and priorities 

• Validate installation conformity with imec’s standards and guidelines through reviews, inspections and supporting records 

• Provide safety oversight and follow up contractor actions on safety and quality findings 

• Keep internal stakeholders and external partners informed 

• Escalate risks and non-conformities, track corrective actions and review evidence for installation acceptance 

Who you are
 
 

• You have a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or Electromechanical Engineering.  

• You have at least 5 years of relevant technical experience.  

• You have experience overseeing contractor-led technical projects and reviewing installations against defined standards and guidelines.  

• You communicate openly and proactively with both internal customers and external partners about the status of ongoing work, and you escalate issues promptly when needed.  

• You adapt easily to changes and time pressure and combine a practical mindset with a strong focus on safety, quality and conformity.  

• You are fluent in English and Spanish.

What you will do
 

IMEC performs world-leading research in nano-electronics, operating a diverse equipment set of most advanced semiconductor wafer processing models. To improve and further roll out our CIM application landscape, we have started the Smart Fab initiative in 2024. Smart Fab is not only about simplification of manual work, it also will deliver more insight into capacity utilization, as well as product quality. You will become part of this journey in a growing team, providing opportunities in an exciting environment.
 
 

• As a member of our Smart Fab team, you will closely work with business analysts and software developers for our equipment integration solution. You will be supported by dedicated test engineers. 

• You will receive industry specific training and can rely on experienced teammates. 

• You perform the crucial task of analyzing how our equipment integration software platform can implement business requirements. The specifications to be passed on to internal and more often external developers can range from straightforward configuration to additional logic to be defined. 

• Some business requirements will result in equipment integration being dependent on related configuration or even features to be implemented in adjacent applications, especially the MES. You thus will gain sufficient knowledge about adjacent CIM applications to effectively collaborate with their business analysts and functional analysts. 

• You have an active role in test preparation and debugging. You will be supported by our PMO team during all phases of the software lifecycle. 

Who you are
 
 

• You have a master’s degree in engineering, exact sciences, or equal by experience. 

• You bring 5 years or more of experience in a complex manufacturing environment, characterized by demanding processes, high product mix, and delicate materials. 

• Prior experience in, or knowledge of, semiconductor manufacturing is a strong asset, preferably in a 300 mm Fab. 

• You have participated in a CIM project, understanding concepts like the automation pyramid and equipment state engines, as well as standards like OPC or SECS. 

• You have strong analytical skills and are solution oriented. You can challenge assumptions and question approaches. 

• You can work independently and in a team. You do work diligently and are dependable. 

• You feel comfortable in a complex environment. 

• Since you will be working in a highly international environment and will be maintaining a good contact with colleagues and co-workers from all over the world, fluency in English is essential.

What you will do
 

IMEC performs world-leading research in nano-electronics, operating a diverse equipment set of most advanced semiconductor wafer processing models. To improve and further roll out our CIM application landscape, we have started the Smart Fab initiative in 2024. Smart Fab is not only about simplification of manual work, it also will deliver more insight into capacity utilization, as well as product quality. You will become part of this journey in a growing team, providing opportunities in an exciting environment. 
 
 

• As a member of our Smart Fab team, you will closely work with equipment engineers and software developers.  

• You will receive industry specific training and can rely on experienced teammates.  

• You will follow Fab Operations to understand the different levels of automation currently implemented in our cleanrooms.  

• Your initial task will be the verification of equipment to host communication as specified during purchasing. Semiconductor equipment communication follows a comprehensive set of standards. However, these standards allow for differences in implementation and scope definition which often cause complications with equipment integration.  

• Once more experienced, you will play a decisive role in exploring equipment behavior at the communication interfaces under different operational scenarios.  

• Your test results are not just necessary for bug fixing. They are crucial input for equipment integration developers in the first place.  

• You will contribute to improving our test methodology, utilizing dedicated test software as well as equipment simulators. 

Who you are
 
 

• You bring 5 years or more of experience in software development and testing, specifically related to hardware automation.  

• Prior experience in, or knowledge of, semiconductor manufacturing is a strong asset, preferably in a 300 mm Fab.  

• You did apply concepts like the automation pyramid and equipment state engines, as well as standards like OPC or SECS. You understand the difference between instructions and reports. You know how to analyze data exchange with hardware units and debug communication issues.  

• You have strong analytical skills, are self-critical, and solution oriented.  

• You can work independently and in a team. You do work diligently and are persistent.  

• Prior experience in a cooperative setup, original software supplier's engineers sharing the workload with in-house developers, as well as onsite-remote hybrid collaboration, is highly desired.  

• You feel comfortable in a complex environment.  

• Since you will be working in a highly international environment and will be maintaining a good contact with colleagues and co-workers from all over the world, fluency in English is essential.

What you will do
 

You will be a member of the Defect Inspection Engineer team (DIE) which is part of the Inspection and Metrology Characterization group (IMC). The IMC group is responsible for the metrology and defectivity process portfolio and tools and follows up processes under evaluation/validation for furture needs. As process engineer in the DIE team, you will be responsible for tools and processes:
 
 

• Process & tool qualification, monitor stability, implement improvements for improved quality and cycle time. 

• Troubleshooting defectivity related issues reported by the First Line Support which cannot be resolved by themselves. 

• Analyze data utilizing sound statistical methods and present summaries to peers and management. 

• Fulfill requests for new applications and create the tool recipes. 

• Investigate tool and recipe issues, focus on root cause analysis and development of long-term solutions. 

• Utilizing expert interpersonal skills, collaborate in a dynamic multidisciplinary and multicultural environment in close cooperation with researchers, hardware engineers, operations, industry assignees, device and process experts. 

• As opportunities arise, innovate new techniques of characterization that align with the Imec’s technology roadmap. 

• You will work in two shifts (early/late) including one weekend out of four (Sa/Su), to support the 24h by 7d fab. 

Who you are
 
 

• You obtained a Master in Science or Engineering or equal by experience and display strong engineering skills and mindset. 

• Experience in a FAB environment is a strong asset. 

• You are data driven and seek out information before making decisions and taking action. 

• You like to work autonomously, well organized, with good attention to detail and set high standards for quality. 

• You speak fluent English. 

• As you will work in cross functional teams, strong communication and reporting skills are required. You are a team player with strong drive to share your expertise and knowledge with colleagues. You strive to document and report.

Join imec’s center of excellence for hardware-software-technology co-design to architect and design the future of technology-aware compute systems.
 

Compute System Architecture (CSA) is a center of excellence at imec for hardware-software-technology co-design for future compute systems. We work in close collaboration with other expertise centers in imec specializing in applications, technology, circuits and design to innovate and pathfind next-generation compute system architectures across multiple domains – AI, HPC, Automotive, Space, and more. CSA has presence in 6 centers of IMEC, in Belgium, Netherlands, Germany, UK, USA and Qatar. This position is primarily for Leuven, Belgium. 
We are looking for a 
Virtual Platform R&D Engineer to develop, enable, and maintain our baseline platform across functional models, complex simulation environments, and towards RTL prototyping. This role sits at the intersection of
 compute system architectures, system simulation, and HW/SW engineering.  
 

What you will do
 
 

• Develop, maintain and stitch virtual platforms together for complex SoC architectures, enabling architectural exploration, and system validation.  

• Build and integrate functional and performance models of compute, memory, interconnect and accelerators across multiple abstraction levels.  

• Implement the required interfaces between simulation infrastructures and support tooling to improve productivity, scalability, and model fidelity.  

• Support workload mapping and enable functional models bring-up on various execution platforms such as: QEMU, gem5, RTL, FGPA.  

• Model and simulate new architectures to analyze critical trade-offs and bottlenecks.  

• Contribute to project definitions and the technical scope of work (timeline, work packages, milestones, deliverables) in cooperation with senior members, if needed.   

• Supervise or assist in mentoring students when necessary.  

Who you are
 
 

• You hold a Master’s or PhD in Electrical/Electronics/Computer Engineering/Science or other relevant domains with hands-on in compute system architectures.   

• You have a deep understanding of system-level design, modern compute and memory systems, and SoC components coupled with performance analysis skills.  

• You have proven expertise, both as a user and as a developer, with simulation frameworks or virtual platforms, such as: QEMU, gem5 or SystemC-based models.  

• You understand the boundaries of hardware and software, but you also understand how to model hardware.  

• You are a hands-on engineer; you have a research-oriented mindset with an inherited curiosity in compute system architectures.  

• You are proficient in C/C++, in bash and scripting (e.g. Python).  

• You have experience in RISC-V-based architecture.   

• You are open-minded, and flexible in accommodating changing priorities to support business needs.   

• You are a team player, as you will be part of a dynamic and distributed team.  

• You are fluent in English and you have strong communication skills, enabling effective collaboration across a multicultural team.

What you will do
 

IMEC performs world-leading research in nano-electronics, operating a diverse equipment set of most advanced semiconductor wafer processing models. To improve and further roll out our CIM application landscape, we have started the Smart Fab initiative in 2024. Smart Fab is not only about simplification of manual work, it also will deliver more insight into capacity utilization, as well as product quality. You will become part of this journey in a growing team, providing opportunities for your career development. 
 
 

• As a member of our Fab Engineering team, you will closely work with experts of the MES and related software – commonly referred to as CIM.  

• You have an active role throughout the entire equipment lifecycle, from automation specification during procurement, to requirement gathering after commissioning, to operational improvement after production release. You make sure that operations and engineering requirements regarding CIM integration are sufficiently specified and can be implemented accordingly. To enable this implementation, you need to understand equipment behavior and communication capabilities – which frequently requires exploration and diligent testing.  

• While technical knowledge and interest is crucial to be successful in this job, you will collaborate with hardware and software engineers who either deliver details to you or must pick up conclusions made by you. Data Specialist is a pivotal role, putting equipment communication capabilities into practice.  

• Commonly known as Industry 4.0 features, in semiconductor manufacturing such equipment communication feeds applications like MES, SPC, FDC (Fault Detection and Classification), APC (Advanced Process Control), and AMHS (Automated Material Handling).  

• With this open position we are specifically looking for candidates who will work with Metrology equipment, i.e. measuring process results and product properties.  

Who you are
 
 

• You have a master’s degree in engineering, exact sciences, or equal by experience.  

• You bring 5 years or more of experience in a complex manufacturing environment, characterized by demanding processes, high product mix, and delicate materials.  

• Prior experience in or knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing is a strong asset, preferably in a 300 mm Fab.  

• You have participated in CIM projects, understanding concepts like the automation pyramid and equipment state engines, as well as standards like OPC or SECS.  

• You understand measurement techniques, why different equipment is needed to measure different properties, and how measurement results can be reported.  

• You have a pro-active approach and are solution oriented. You cannot wait to roll up your sleeves and dive right into the action. You easily work independently and are an effective team player as well.  

• You thrive in a complex and demanding environment.  

• Since you will be working in a highly international environment and will be maintaining a good contact with colleagues and co-workers from all over the world, fluency in English is essential.

Shape the architecture behind the next generation of AI supercomputers.
 

Join imec and design the future of AI computing
 

What if your architectural decisions could influence the future of artificial intelligence at the scale of the world's most advanced computing systems?
At imec, you will work at the intersection of AI, semiconductor innovation, and large-scale computing architectures. Together with leading experts in computing systems, chip technology, software, and artificial intelligence, you will help define how future AI infrastructure is built, optimized, and scaled.
This is not a product maintenance role. It is an opportunity to explore breakthrough architectures that could shape the next decade of AI and high-performance computing.
 

What you will do
 

As a Principal AI & High-Performance Computing Architect, you will drive innovation across the entire computing stack, from AI applications and system software to processors, accelerators, and semiconductor technologies.
You will create models, simulations, and design explorations that help identify the most promising paths toward future AI computing systems that deliver significant improvements in performance, energy efficiency, and sustainability.
Your responsibilities include:
 
 

• Exploring architectural solutions for next-generation AI and high-performance computing clusters. 

• Analysing the behaviour and performance characteristics of large-scale AI workloads. 

• Developing performance models that identify bottlenecks and opportunities for innovation. 

• Evaluating future processor, accelerator, memory, and system designs. 

• Collaborating with experts in computer architecture, AI, semiconductor technology, system software, and modelling. 

• Defining requirements for future AI computing platforms and processor architectures. 

• Guiding strategic research directions through data-driven performance analysis and projections. 

• Contributing to breakthrough innovations that improve performance, energy efficiency, operational cost, and environmental impact. 

Who you are
 
 

• Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or relevant STEM degree, with at least around 8 years of experience.   

• Experience with performance analysis, engineering, and optimization of HPC applications, such as molecular dynamics and computational fluid dynamics,  

• Experience in AI for HPC is a plus.   

• Experience with distributed AI/ML applications, such as LLM training and inference.   

• Experience in system performance modeling ranging from a single device (e.g. a GPU) to a machine scale (e.g. a cluster).  

• Good understanding of GPU (preferably XPU) system architectures, distributed programming models, runtime resource management, and microarchitecture.   

• Strong programming ability in C++ and Python. CUDA knowledge is considered a plus.   

• Your communication and interpersonal skills enable you to work in a dynamic, distributed team. You actively share experiences and knowledge with colleagues. A history of mentoring more junior engineers and interns is a huge plus.   

• We are looking for your excellent communication skills in English, as you will work in a multicultural team and together with our partners.

What you will do 
 
 

• As a member of our Smart Fab team, you will closely work with developers of the same and adjacent software applications, Functional Analysts, and Business Analysts, to deliver a modern CIM application landscape.  

• Your primary contact will be the developer team lead, responsible for establishing our in-house development capability for the commercially sourced Equipment Integration platform, and we will assign an additional mentor during your onboarding.  

• You will follow Fab Operations to understand the different levels of automation currently implemented in our cleanrooms.  

• Your initial tasks will be configuration of existing equipment controller software modules, followed by developing clones of software modules for the same equipment type.  

• As we insource more functionality of the commercially sourced Equipment Integration platform, you will start developing equipment controller software modules for new equipment types. You will also be involved in developing custom solutions interfacing with the commercial platform.  

• You will participate in equipment model testing, both with software emulators as well as physical connection to the equipment hardware.  

Who you are 
 
 

• You bring 5 years or more of experience in software development, specifically related to hardware automation, and performing Java OOP.  

• Prior experience in, or knowledge of, semiconductor manufacturing is a strong asset, preferably in a 300 mm Fab.  

• You understand concepts like the automation pyramid and equipment state engines, as well as standards like OPC or SECS.  

• You can work independently and in a team. You do work diligently and are persistent.  

• Prior experience in a cooperative setup, original software supplier's engineers sharing the workload with in-house developers, as well as onsite-remote hybrid collaboration, is highly desired.  

• You feel comfortable in a complex and demanding environment.  

• Since you will be working in a highly international environment and will be maintaining a good contact with colleagues and co-workers from all over the world, fluency in English is essential.

What you will do 
 

You will join our SEM-TEM operations team within the FAB, where we perform both in-line and out-of-line electron microscopy inspections. These inspections are essential at various stages of process development, enabling us to characterise materials and processes at wafer level with a high degree of precision. By delivering accurate and timely insights, we support our internal customers in developing innovative chip manufacturing processes that meet ever more demanding requirements. To achieve this, we rely on cutting-edge cleanroom facilities and highly advanced equipment. In this role, you will help ensure the health, quality and reliability of our microscopy tools through close collaboration with equipment suppliers and internal users. In short, you will support the teams carrying out microscopy analyses and contribute to the smooth and high-quality execution of SEM and TEM inspections. 
 
 

• As a SEM/TEM Hardware Assistant Technician, your key responsibilities will include:  

• Monitoring and following up on the overall health and performance of the tools.  

• Acting as the main point of contact with equipment suppliers to report, discuss and resolve tool-related issues.  

• Serving as the first point of contact for internal users when tool health or performance issues arise.  

• Contributing to the achievement of hardware performance targets and key performance indicators (KPIs).  

• Supporting statistical process control (SPC) activities for TEM tools to help maintain stable and reliable performance.  

Who you are 
 
 

• You hold a bachelor’s degree in a scientific field such as physics, engineering, chemistry, or another relevant discipline. (or equivalent by relevant experience)  

• Hands-on experience with laboratory tools, microscopy equipment or micromachining systems would be a strong advantage.  

• You are well organised, able to plan effectively, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where multitasking and setting priorities are essential.  

• You are a communicative team player with a good command of English.  

• You are willing to work in a shift system, including early, late and night shifts, (24/7) as well as one weekend in four.

 Apply today via 09 218 79 35 or talentcenter40@randstad.be to join the team of Logent.

Satellit is seeking an experienced .NET developer with Java know-how to join a multi-disciplinary team delivering digital identity and authentication capabilities for a major energy-sector engagement. The role involves building, validating and documenting reusable authentication/authorization components, contributing to deployment automation, collaborating with IT stakeholders, and participating in agile squad activities. This position follows a hybrid work model with an expectation of being on-site about two days per week and is planned to start in the mid-October to mid-November timeframe. Full-time commitment is required.
Who are you?

Skills & competences:

• Autonomy

• Teamwork

• Presentation skills

• Communication

• Continuous learning

• Technical documentation

• Analytical problem solving

• Resilience

• Versatility and adaptability

• Continuous integration and deployment practices

• Agile methodologies and Scrum

What will you do?

• Design, implement, unit-test and document libraries, services or components that handle user authentication and authorization.

• Create example applications and code samples to illustrate how to integrate identity and access services into new or existing systems, and communicate these to engineering teams.

• Customize and extend commercial or open-source products (for example access managers, authorization engines, API gateways, reverse proxies and directory services) and produce supporting documentation for those extensions.

• Work closely with IT and application teams to identify integration points, diagnose issues, and resolve problems when connecting to identity Fabric services.

• Take part in squad sprint activities, including planning, execution and retrospective work.
